
**Fix:** add those six paths to `core:` in `.github/workflows/ci.yml`. That is a governed `ci.yml` edit, which the claim (6496953999) excluded and which needs the maintainer's ruling. The alternative is the dev's option B (ui package-level `turbo.json` files, no `ci.yml` edit), which the report measured and rejected. The seat put the choice to the maintainer in its session chat, recommending the `core:` addition.

Gate-derivation gap, noted for the record: the dev's `dispatch-gates --commands` run (report 6498038778) did not derive `check:ci-filter-parity` for a `turbo.json` diff. If that is a missing family mapping, a card follows.

A diff confined to one of them now starts `build-core`, `test-plan`/`test` (ORed with `crosspkg`) and, on push, the jobs that read `core`. Every one of the six was already under the `ui` filter (`ui/**`), so the ui jobs ran on them before and still do.

The seat record should say in so many words that the approval predates the governed hunks and that the landing click stays the maintainer's. Not a finding against the tree.

Not blocking: the gate itself ran red then green on this PR.

Named gates: `Lint · CI, release & engine gates` (hosts `check:ci-filter-parity`, red on `47d8611899`) `success`; `Lint · repo & tooling gates` (hosts the shared-module self-tests, the Step-collector gate and the Self-test wiring gate) `success`; `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `PR-body guards`, `Build Core`, `Test Core` 8/8, `Test UI` 16/16, `Type Check UI`, `Lint UI`, `Build & E2E UI`, `Live E2E UI`, all four `Type Check ·` lanes, all eight `Lint ·` lanes, `filter` — `success`.

The gate derives the required set as turbo.json itself + `globalDependencies` + every `$TURBO_ROOT$/...` input of a build task `pnpm build` (`turbo run build --filter=!@objectstack/docs`) runs, and covers a path only when a `core` entry contains it verbatim or a `prefix/**` of its literal segments. Each of the six new rows is the verbatim string of its `$TURBO_ROOT$` input, so coverage is by the sound limb, not by a pattern match the gate refuses to make; `ui/scripts/vite-*.ts` is one glob in both files and picomatch (the paths-filter matcher) reads `*` within one segment exactly as turbo does. The leftover rule is untouched: every new row is itself a declared build input. Placement is inside the BUILD INPUTS block, before the BUILD CORE'S GUARDS rows, with a comment whose claim I checked — the generic `build` task is the one every workspace package runs (`pnpm-workspace.yaml` lists `ui`, `ui/packages/*`, `ui/apps/*`, `ui/examples/*`), so a diff confined to one of the six moves Build Core's hashes. Scenario: a diff confined to one of the six now schedules Build Core and Test Core on the PR, and `check:ci-filter-parity` is green by parity (120/120 on this head; 5/120 red on `47d8611899`). Test Core is scheduled by `core`/`crosspkg`, and no gate subject reads the generic `test` task's root inputs (`vitest.preset.mts` sits in `core:` by hand). So a diff confined to one of the five moves every `@objectstack/*#test` hash but starts Test Core first in the merge queue — the ruling's shape, one task over. No stale replay results (the hash moves; `ui/**` runs Test UI on the PR; the queue runs Test Core with `core` true), the ruling scoped six build rows, and the parity gate demanded none of these, so this is not a defect of the hunk; it is the next card: either a fourth parity subject for `test` inputs plus the five rows, or a recorded decision that Test Core's scheduling does not follow generic test inputs.

**`.github/workflows/lint.yml` — holds.** Judged against `scripts/check-self-test-wired.mjs` (`INVOCATION_RE` consumes the directory prefix, so the new `core:` row `ui/scripts/invoked-as.mjs` is a named path; the file exists and its code carries `--self-test`, L322, so it joins the population and must be run), `scripts/check-step-collectors.mjs` (`SCRIPT_TOKEN` accepts a path under any directory, so the harness plants the stub at `ui/scripts/invoked-as.mjs`, distinct from the root twin's `scripts/invoked-as.mjs` — no basename collision), and `ui/scripts/invoked-as.mjs` itself (imports `node:` builtins only, so the step needs no ui install; the job checks out the whole tree with `fetch-depth: 0`). The over-selection the gate's header owns up to (a paths-filter row is read as CI naming the script) bought a real run: the ui copy's 12-case self-test had no CI runner before.
